timeline: You have likely never heard how the ghost lights of West Bengal lure fishermen into deep swamps and trap them forever.
Local villagers call this strange phenomenon Aleya.
These hovering lights look just like a distant lantern held by a friend.
Tradition says they are the wandering spirits of fishermen who died on these very waters.
When a lone traveler tries to follow them toward safety, the lights dance away.
They lead victims deeper into bottomless bogs until they vanish completely.
Modern science offers a more grounded explanation for the ghostly glow.
Researchers point to phosphine and methane gas produced by organic decay in the mud.
Yet even with chemistry at play, locals refuse to walk the marshes after dark.
